top_choice_rationale: Buchwald and Hartwig developed ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed C-N coupling. Making the Pd-amido C-N reductive elimination fast through bulky, electron-rich ligand design is a different mechanistic problem from the C-C couplings honoured in 2010. Both laureates worked out the catalytic cycle independently, and the method has more than 25 years of independent confirmation and routine use in synthesis and process chemistry. It has the cleanest two-name attribution on the slate and five explicit supporters, and Kosugi's tin-amide work was a narrow, stoichiometric precursor. Among the degradation proposals I prefer P003 over P004, because Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are chemical design. The glue strand through Handa is a serendipitous discovery explained afterwards. Condensates (P002) rank above no award but remain borderline chemistry with unsettled scope.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, or any other proposed laureate, though as the only synthetic organic chemist I may be biased toward P001
